approximations: mitsuba: alpha-masked shapes use the `volpath` integrator (its emitter sampling passes shadow rays through a mask BSDF per point; `path` would treat the cut-out part as an occluder).

mitsuba: absorption-only interior media use the `volpath` integrator (same max_depth and rr_depth rules as `path`); homogeneous medium with sigma_t = -ln(T)/depth per RGB channel (written as scale = max sigma and rgb = sigma / max sigma, because an `rgb` medium value must lie in [0, 1]), albedo 0.
mitsuba: directional light angularRadius is ignored (delta direction).
mitsuba: material 'screen': alpha_mode mask: cut out where opacity 1 x base colour alpha (texture) < cutoff 0.5
coverage: mitsuba: material 'screen': specular_weight/specular_color scale F0 only through an IOR of 1.0000 (OpenPBR scales F at both ends)
mitsuba: material 'screen': base colour texture 'screen' (128x128, sRGB, wrap repeat): bitmap bilinear, level 0 only

mitsuba: material 'screen': alpha mask: Mitsuba's mask BSDF is a stochastic opacity, so it reads a 0/255 bitmap of (opacity x alpha >= 0.5) evaluated 8x finer than the texture with the same bilinear interpolation (contour exact to 0.063 texel); the shape needs volpath for shadow rays to pass through
